Subject: Retainer bucket + top-up terms — Atlas Health

Hi Natalie — great to meet yesterday. Following up with a concise framing of the pricing structure we discussed so your procurement team can review: 

Summary (high level)
- Monthly retainer (reserved bucket): Atlas picks a $/month retainer that gives you a guaranteed token bucket with soft priority for capacity.
- Top-ups (burst/one-off): When daily usage exceeds the reserved bucket, on-demand top-ups are applied at a higher per-token on-demand rate. Top-ups settle monthly.
- Overage / fallback: If reserved capacity is exhausted, Redwood will route extra traffic to on-demand at the top-up rate unless you enable a hard reject.

Key negotiation levers we can move:
1) Minimum monthly retainer (floor) — reduces on-demand rate and unlocks volume discount tiers.
2) On-demand top-up premium — typically 1.6–2.2x hosted per-token list rate depending on retainer level.
3) Annual true-up / lookback — smoothing mechanism to reconcile actual vs committed.
4) Grace burst buffer — short-term credit for spiky launches (one-time concession we can include in fast-start deals).

Next asks for procurement:
- Target min monthly spend Atlas is comfortable committing to (ballpark is fine).
- Expected 90th-percentile daily tokens for month 1 and month 6 (we attached the usage projection template).
- Any required billing/legal language (SOW, PO process, standard redlines).

Attached: redwood_retainer_bucket_v2.pdf (pricing bands + example math), usage_projection_atlas.xlsx (simple template).

If this looks reasonable I can propose two concrete options: a conservative starter retainer (lower floor, higher top-up%) and an enterprise retainer (higher floor, discounted top-up and quarterly true-up). Happy to run numbers once you give a target floor.

Thanks — Olga

1) When you say the top-up rate is 1.6–2.2x, is that a multiplier on your hosted public list per-token price? We need the absolute $/1k-token numbers for budget planning.
2) We usually need a minimum monthly floor to be expressed as an annual commitment/ASL for internal chargeback. Could you show us the effective blended price at $25k/mo vs $75k/mo?

Proposed quick responses:
- Provide blended example math, show top-up absolute $/1k for each tier (I can draft).

Olga — sounds reasonable. A couple of finance guardrails: 
- 1.8x on top-ups for $25k floor: acceptable as an introductory offer but cap total discretionary credits to $10k in Q4 (so the 20% rebate must be scoped against that cap).
- 1.4x for $75k floor: agrees with volume-discount logic; ensure we show blended $/1k in the doc (finance likes the effective rate).
- Regional pinning: ops can support region routing but add an SLA note that routing to a single region may slightly increase the chance of soft throttling during infra incidents.

Karthik — loop in you for any pricing incentives you think we should hold back for later stages. Otherwise I approve sending an OPTIONS email with the two floors and the spike rebate (subject to cap).

— Vivek

Natalie — thanks for the quick questions. Below are the concrete numbers and an options table (see attached PDF for the math).

Option A — Starter retainer
- Floor: $25,000 / month (reserved bucket)
- Effective per-1k-token list price: $0.90 (hosted list)
- Top-up (on-demand) multiplier: 1.8x -> Top-up price $1.62 per 1k tokens
- True-up: Quarterly lookback, month-by-month reconciliation
- Launch spike concession: 7-day 20% rebate on top-ups; finance cap $10k (applies during agreed launch window)

Option B — Enterprise retainer
- Floor: $75,000 / month (reserved bucket)
- Effective per-1k-token list price: $0.90 (hosted list) with tiered discounts -> blended effective $/1k: $0.68
- Top-up (on-demand) multiplier: 1.4x -> Top-up price $1.26 per 1k tokens
- True-up: Monthly or quarterly (customer preference)
- Launch spike concession: 7-day 30% rebate on top-ups; finance cap $25k

Other notes:
- Region pinning: We will restrict top-ups to us-east upon request; ops will add routing flag and include a short SLA caveat.
- Billing: invoices itemize reserved bucket, top-ups, and any applied rebates.

If this matches what procurement needs I can convert to a single-page options sheet and an initial SOW addendum for legal. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer a walkthrough.

Best — Olga
